record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: What space-time development of strong-interaction processes generates scale-invariant fluctuations, and how do parton fragmentation, resonance production and decay, quantum interference effects, and dynamical quark-gluon phase transitions interact in the overall intermittency phenomenon; is the answer simple, or is intermittency the physics of a complex system?

evidence.quote: 7. Intermittency and the space-time structure of Strong Interactions. On the theoretical side of the problem, a much better understanding of the space-time development of the processes is required[18].

The extension of the interactions to large distances, which is probably necessary to generate scale-invariant fluctuations, is the origin of most (if not all) open questions: what is the interplay between parton fragmentation, resonance production and decay, quantum interference effects, dynamical quark-gluon phase transitions, in the overall phenomenon? Is there a simple answer or do we face the physics of a complex system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In high-energy multiparticle production, the scaled factorial moments F_q(δ) of the distribution of charged-particle multiplicities in phase-space cells of size δ are observed to grow as a power of 1/δ when δ → 0 (the "intermittency" phenomenon), indicating scale-invariant (self-similar) fluctuations over a range of resolutions.

Provide a theoretical description of the space-time development of strong-interaction processes that accounts for these scale-invariant fluctuations. Specifically:

(a) Identify a dynamical mechanism whose extension to large space-time distances produces the observed power-law scaling of F_q(δ).

(b) Determine quantitatively the interplay among the following contributing mechanisms in generating the overall intermittency signal:
 (i) perturbative and non-perturbative parton fragmentation (QCD cascades and hadronization),
 (ii) resonance production and subsequent decays,
 (iii) quantum interference effects, including Bose–Einstein correlations among identical bosons,
 (iv) dynamical quark–gluon phase transitions (e.g., deconfinement or chiral transitions) that may induce critical-type fluctuations.

(c) Decide whether the observed intermittency admits a single dominant, simple explanation in terms of one of these mechanisms, or whether it is an emergent property of a complex multi-component system requiring all of the above ingredients on an equal footing.

A complete answer should specify the predicted intermittency exponents (anomalous dimensions) φ_q from the proposed space-time picture and confront them with the experimental scaling behavior of F_q(δ) in leptonic, hadronic, and nuclear collisions.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the space-time origin of intermittency in soft hadronic processes and the relative roles of parton cascades, resonance decays, Bose–Einstein interference, and possible QCD phase transitions. Reviews of intermittency in multiparticle production discuss self-similar QCD parton showers, models with phase transitions, and statistical field theory of density fluctuations, but no unified, quantitatively complete space-time picture has been established. The question remains an open conceptual problem in soft QCD phenomenology.

status_evidence.title: Intermittency and particle correlations: Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Experimental data on particle correlations and fluctuations in high-energy multiparticle collisions show evidence for scaling-law evolution in small phase-space domains.
status_evidence.claim: Intermittency is well-established experimentally but its theoretical interpretation involves multiple mechanisms.

status_evidence.title: Intermittency in multiparticle production at high energy
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews self-similar cascading, QCD parton showers, models with phase transitions, and statistical field theory of multiparticle density fluctuations.
status_evidence.claim: Several competing mechanisms have been proposed without a single unified resolution.

status_evidence.title: Intermittency in and the fractal nature of nuclear fragmentation: A critical examination
status_evidence.snippet: Scale-invariance and intermittency ideas are relevant for both multiparticle production and nuclear multifragmentation processes.
status_evidence.claim: The full interplay of mechanisms is unresolved.
